internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The consonantal root ه-و-ي surfaces in the Quran as at least two internally coherent but mutually unbridged lexical classes plus a resistant singleton. (1) A MOTION class: هَوَىٰ/تَهْوِي/أَهْوَىٰ/هَاوِيَة = a downward departure — to fall, set, plunge, be swept/cast down, or perish (star setting 53:1; ruin under wrath 20:81; wind-borne plunge 22:31; causative overthrow 53:53; the Pit 101:9). Its imperfect is the i-stem تَهْوِي. (2) A DESIRE class: the noun هَوَىٰ/أَهْوَآء (27 tokens) = the self's ungoverned inclination invoked as an authority against revealed guidance (object of ٱتَّبَعَ, qualified بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ/بِغَيْرِ هُدًى, set opposite ٱلْحَقّ/ٱلْعِلْم/ٱلْهُدَىٰ, even idolized 25:43/45:23), with its finite a-stem verb تَهْوَىٰ = 'the nafs craves' (2:87, 5:70, 53:23). The i-stem/a-stem imperfect split (تَهْوِي vs تَهْوَىٰ) is itself internal evidence of two distinct Form-I verbs. No verse Quran-internally glosses desire as a fall or welds the two poles; the sole candidate bridge (14:37 تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِم, hearts 'incline/rush toward') is undetermined between the two verbs, and 20:16 reaches for a different root (فَتَرْدَىٰ, rdy) to say 'perish' beside desire. A lone nominal 14:43 هَوَآء ('hearts are empty air/void') fits neither class. Because the bridge across MOTION and DESIRE is not demonstrated internally and 14:43 is an unbridged singleton, the honest result is a multi-class UNRESOLVED root, not a single nucleus.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Across all classes hwy does NOT entail: upward/ascending or self-propelled willed locomotion (every physical use is downward and yielded-to or imposed — gravity/set 53:1, wind 22:31, wrath 20:81, devils 6:71, divine overthrow 53:53); a mere initial drop (22:31 distinguishes خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ from تَهْوِي بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ to a remote مَكَانٍ سَحِيقٍ, adding transport to a terminus); knowledge-based or warranted motive (the desire noun is structurally بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ 30:29/6:119, بِغَيْرِ هُدًى 28:50, عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ 5:48); a neutral/approved volition in the noun (هَوَىٰ/أَهْوَآء is uniformly the wrong standard, restrained at 79:40 نَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ); an intrinsic moral category in the fall verb (53:1 the star's setting is morally neutral); and emptiness/void (only 14:43, which conversely entails neither fall nor desire). Same root ≠ one meaning is instantiated internally: the identical surface هَوَىٰ (hawaY`) is tagged N 'desire' (18:28, 25:43) and V 'fell/set' (20:81, 53:1).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 14:43 وَأَفْـِٔدَتُهُمْ هَوَآءٌ ('their hearts are empty air/void') carries neither downward fall nor self-inclination; it is a morphologically distinct singleton (هَوَاء, not the caprice-plural أَهْوَاء) that attaches to no other occurrence Quran-internally, blocking any single root nucleus.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A single unified nucleus 'yielding to a directional/downward pull toward a terminus' (fall physically ≈ heart dropping-toward = desire), anchored on 14:37 (the i-stem fall verb تَهْوِي governing directional إِلَى for the heart's inclination) and the recurrent caprice→ruin resolution (20:16 فَتَرْدَىٰ; 38:26 فَيُضِلَّكَ; adjacency of 20:81 فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ). This is rejected as not decisively demonstrated: the a-stem/i-stem verb split marks two lexemes, 14:37 is itself semantically undetermined (positive, prayed-for, directional — unlike the pejorative desire noun and unlike the downward fall verb), 20:16 uses a separate root (rdy) for 'perish', and 14:43 (void) is covered by neither pole; the unifying gloss risks being the everything-fitting abstraction the methodology warns against and leans on external etymology the source policy bars.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses (A bottom-up, B derivational, C adversarial) independently partition the data the same way and independently conclude the cross-class unification is not Quran-internally established. MOTION (5 occ., all downward, incl. causative IV 53:53 and participle 101:9) and DESIRE (27 noun + 3 a-stem verb, uniform ٱتَّبَعَ/ٱتَّخَذَ/نَهَىٰ عَن frame against عِلْم/هُدًى/حَقّ) are each internally CONSISTENT and narrow, but nothing internal bridges them: no verse glosses desire as a fall, the imperfect vowel split (تَهْوِي vs تَهْوَىٰ) evidences two distinct Form-I verbs, and 20:16 chooses rdy (فَتَرْدَىٰ) rather than hwy for the 'perish' that follows desire. The only cross-pole hinge (14:37) is unresolvable from internal evidence, and 14:43 (void) is unbridged to either class. Under the rule that two or more senses with no Quran-internal bridge force UNRESOLVED, and preferring the narrowest account over a forced unity, the root is reported as multi-class UNRESOLVED with per-class dispositions and the seams persisted as hard cases.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: (For a nafs) to crave/incline toward — the a-stem finite verb تَهْوَىٰ, subject always the self/souls; valence neutral but the content is contested (rejected messengers 2:87/5:70; vain conjecture 53:23).
clusters.classification_rationale: Three occurrences share the a-stem imperfect تَهْوَىٰ (distinct from the i-stem fall verb تَهْوِي) with nafs/anfus as subject, cohering as the finite verb of the DESIRE noun class; morphologically separated from the MOTION verbs.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Hearts inclining/rushing toward — the one occurrence where the i-stem fall verb morphology (تَهْوِي, like 22:31) governs directional إِلَى to mean a (positive, prayed-for) leaning toward, undetermined between the MOTION and DESIRE poles.
clusters.classification_rationale: 14:37 تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ is the sole potential bridge between MOTION and DESIRE, but it is unresolvable from internal evidence: morphologically the fall verb, semantically an inclination, and pragmatically positive (a supplication) — unlike both the downward fall and the pejorative desire noun. clusters.classification_rationale: 6:71 ٱسْتَهْوَتْهُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ is the only Form-X token; it straddles the two poles (make-fall vs solicit-desire) and its exact force is underdetermined by the packet, so it is recorded as a structural boundary rather than assigned.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 6:71 كَٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَهْوَتْهُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ: the Form-X causative blends 'lured to fall/go astray' with 'made to follow desire', resisting a clean placement in either the MOTION or DESIRE class.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Empty air / hollow void — a static vacancy of the heart, entailing neither downward motion nor inclination; a morphologically distinct nominal (هَوَاء, not the caprice-plural أَهْوَاء).
clusters.classification_rationale: 14:43 وَأَفْـِٔدَتُهُمْ هَوَآءٌ resists both major poles simultaneously and connects to no other occurrence Quran-internally; assimilating it ('the air through which one falls') would require forbidden external etymology. resistant_deep_analysis.preliminary_note: Candidate: 'the empty air/medium through which one falls', a possible loose tie to the MOTION class.
resistant_deep_analysis.reconciliation_rationale: No internal corroboration; the tie needs external etymology. Morphologically distinct singleton. Persisted as the primary resistant seam blocking a unified nucleus.

independent_verification: All three lenses (A, B, adversarial C) independently produced the same partition and independently declined to certify a unified nucleus; C explicitly returned RESISTANT for root-unity.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 38 occurrences of ه-و-ي (29 N, 8 V, 1 V[X]) with Tanzil verse_text and QAC morphology; downward-motion verses (53:1, 20:81, 22:31, 53:53, 101:9) vs desire noun/verb verses (27 nominal ٱتَّبَعَ frames + 2:87/5:70/53:23) read directly.
layer_attribution.derivation: i-stem imperfect تَهْوِي (22:31, 14:37) vs a-stem imperfect تَهْوَىٰ (2:87, 5:70, 53:23) mark two distinct Form-I verbs; Form IV أَهْوَىٰ (53:53) and Form X ٱسْتَهْوَىٰ (6:71) are causatives of the fall verb; هَاوِيَة (101:9) is its active participle; هَوَاء (14:43) is a separate nominal from أَهْوَآء.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Two lexicalized classes — MOTION (fall/descend/cast-down family) and DESIRE (هَوَىٰ/أَهْوَآء caprice + a-stem verb) — plus an unbridged nominal singleton (void, 14:43); classes are internally CONSISTENT but not shown to share one meaning.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: DESIRE is framed against هُدًى/عِلْم/حَقّ/وَحْي (28:50, 30:29, 5:48, 53:3) and as idol (25:43/45:23); MOTION is framed by external agents (wind 22:31, wrath 20:81, devils 6:71, divine overthrow 53:53). These contextual/narrative framings are recorded but not elevated into the root claim.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: 14:43 downgraded to RESISTANT after the 'medium-of-falling' candidate failed for lack of internal corroboration; 14:37 and 6:71 downgraded to STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY as undetermined cross-pole cases rather than forced into a class.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The MOTION↔DESIRE bridge is undemonstrated (sole hinge 14:37 ambiguous; 20:16 uses rdy not hwy for 'perish'), and 14:43 (void) is an unbridged singleton; hence the root is UNRESOLVED / multi-class, with 14:43, 14:37, and 6:71 persisted as hard cases.

hard_cases.reason: Void/empty-air heart entails neither downward fall nor self-inclination; a morphologically distinct singleton (هَوَاء, not أَهْوَاء) with no internal tie to either class — the strongest single obstacle to a unified root nucleus.

evidence_basis.statement: 14:43 وَأَفْـِٔدَتُهُمْ هَوَآءٌ ('their hearts are empty air/void') carries neither downward fall nor self-inclination; it is a morphologically distinct singleton (هَوَاء, not the caprice-plural أَهْوَاء) that attaches to no other occurrence Quran-internally, blocking any single root nucleus.

hard_cases.reason: Sole candidate MOTION↔DESIRE bridge (i-stem fall verb تَهْوِي with directional إِلَى for a heart's leaning), but positive, prayed-for, and semantically undetermined — it cannot certify the bridge, leaving the two classes unlinked.

evidence_basis.statement: 14:37 فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ: the i-stem fall verb morphology carries a heart's directional inclination-toward, the sole candidate weld between the fall pole and the desire pole, but its force is undetermined by internal evidence.

hard_cases.reason: Only Form-X token; ٱسْتَهْوَىٰ blends 'caused to fall/go astray' (result حَيْرَان) with 'caused to follow desire', filing cleanly under neither class.

evidence_basis.statement: 6:71 كَٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَهْوَتْهُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ: the Form-X causative blends 'lured to fall/go astray' with 'made to follow desire', resisting a clean placement in either the MOTION or DESIRE class.

hard_case_representation.rationale: The root is reported as multi-class UNRESOLVED. The occurrences that block a single nucleus are persisted as hard cases: 14:43 (void singleton, RESISTANT_SEAM), 14:37 (undetermined cross-pole hinge, ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY), and 6:71 (Form-X fall/desire blend, STRUCTURAL_ATYPICALITY). Each is grounded in occurrence semantics and morphology, not imported lexica.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal occurrence or verse that supplies the missing bridge across the MOTION (fall) and DESIRE (caprice) classes — e.g. a verse that explicitly glosses هَوَىٰ (desire, 18:28/25:43) as a downward fall, or that governs the a-stem desire verb and the i-stem fall verb with a shared act, or that ties 14:43 هَوَاء (void) to either class — which would show the current class-only partition is wrong and a single nucleus is warranted.
rejection_condition.search_location: The DESIRE noun frames (18:28, 25:43, 45:23, 5:48, 30:29, 79:40), the a-stem desire verbs (2:87, 5:70, 53:23), the MOTION verbs (53:1, 22:31, 20:81, 53:53, 101:9), and the seam occurrences 14:37, 6:71, 14:43 — read for any internal cross-reference or shared syntactic act linking the poles.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Compare the i-stem (تَهْوِي, 22:31/14:37) vs a-stem (تَهْوَىٰ, 2:87/5:70/53:23) imperfects and the noun frames; require a verse where the same act or an explicit gloss connects fall and desire without appeal to external lexica; confirm word_refs, qac_pos, and qac_verb_form against the packet.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Reject bridges resting only on shared consonantal skeleton, homography (hawaY` tagged both N-desire and V-fell), or inherited etymology ('desire = inward fall'); 20:16 uses a different root (rdy, فَتَرْدَىٰ) for 'perish' beside desire, so thematic caprice→ruin adjacency does not count as a lexical bridge.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If no such internal bridge is found, the classes remain unbridged and the root stays UNRESOLVED / multi-class (LOCAL, class-only); no universal root nucleus may be asserted.

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal occurrence is found that explicitly links the fall verb (تَهْوِي 22:31 / هَوَىٰ 53:1, 20:81 / أَهْوَىٰ 53:53) to the desire noun هَوَىٰ/أَهْوَآء (e.g. 18:28, 25:43, 5:48) within one act or gloss, reopen the MOTION↔DESIRE bridge and reconsider a single nucleus.

If 14:37 تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ is disambiguated by further internal morphological/syntactic evidence toward either the i-stem fall verb (22:31) or the a-stem desire verb (2:87/5:70/53:23), reopen the hinge and its cluster placement.
If 14:43 هَوَآء (void) can be connected Quran-internally to either the fall class or the desire class by an additional occurrence, reopen the singleton and reassign it out of RESISTANT.
If the Form-X token 6:71 ٱسْتَهْوَتْهُ is shown internally to resolve to either 'cause to fall' (MOTION) or 'cause to follow desire' (DESIRE), reopen its structural-boundary status.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: No universal root nucleus is claimed (claim_scope_kind=UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY), so adversarial refutation of a root-wide gloss is not required. The per-class accounts are each internally CONSISTENT and distinct (i-stem fall verb + causatives + Pit vs a-stem desire verb + هَوَىٰ/أَهْوَآء noun), but their unification is deliberately not asserted; the resistant seams (14:43, 14:37, 6:71) are persisted rather than refuted.
